transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom Business Support. My name is David. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Hi David. My name is Mark Taylor, calling on behalf of Nova Retail Group. Our internet is completely down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm very sorry to hear that, Mr. Taylor. I know how critical connectivity is. I can definitely look into this for you. To access your account, could you please provide your Customer ID?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, it's CUST-2007.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. And for security, could you please verify the 6-digit security PIN on the account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, thank you for verifying. I have the Nova Retail Group account pulled up now. I see you're calling about the fiber broadband service. You said it's completely out?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That's right. It went out about thirty minutes ago. I'm working from home and I'm totally dead in the water here.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand completely. Let's see what's going on. Have you had a chance to try rebooting your equipment yet?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, twice. I unplugged the main fiber box—the ONT—and the Cymbal Wi-Fi router. Waited a minute each time. Nothing changed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, thank you for doing that. That saves us a step. What are the lights on the ONT doing right now?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: The power light is solid green, but the one labeled 'Optical' is blinking red, and there's a red 'Alarm' light on too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it. A red alarm light is definitely an indicator of a problem. I'm going to run a remote signal test to your ONT from my side. It will take about 30 seconds. Do you mind holding for a moment?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. Running the test now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, Mr. Taylor, thank you for your patience. The test failed, which means I'm unable to get any response from your terminal. That confirms what you're seeing on your end—there's a total loss of signal.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So what does that mean?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It often points to an issue outside the premises. Can I ask, have you had any severe weather in your area recently?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Actually, yes. We had a huge thunderstorm roll through about an hour ago. Lots of wind and rain.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a very likely culprit. Before we assume that, I'd like to try one more guided power cycle, just to be absolutely certain it isn't the equipment itself. Would you be willing to do that with me?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Alright, if you think it'll help. What do you need me to do?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please go to the Optical Network Terminal, the main box where the fiber line comes in, and unplug the power cord from the back of it.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay... it's unplugged. All lights are off.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. We're going to leave it unplugged for a full sixty seconds this time to allow the internal components to fully reset. Just let me know when you're ready to plug it back in.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, waiting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While we wait, I'm just checking our network monitoring tools for your area to see if there are any other reported issues.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Find anything?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There are a few other offline devices in your immediate vicinity. This is starting to look like a localized event. Okay, it's been a minute. Please go ahead and plug the power cord back into the ONT.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, it's plugged back in. The power light is on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Now, the device needs about two to three minutes to fully boot up and attempt to connect to our network. We need to watch that 'Optical' or 'PON' light. We want it to go from blinking to solid green.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Alright, I'm watching it. It's blinking green for a moment... now it's back to blinking red.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, let's give it the full three minutes. Sometimes it makes a few attempts.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: This is frustrating. I have a deadline.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand, and I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. We'll get to the bottom of this.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, it's been about three minutes now. Any change with that optical light?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, no change. Still blinking red, and the red Alarm light is on. It's not connecting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. Thank you for doing that, Mr. Taylor. That confirms it. The blinking red light and alarm status, combined with the storm and other outages in your area, indicate a physical break in the fiber optic line.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: A break? You mean the cable is actually cut?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's correct. It's very likely a tree branch came down on the line during the storm. Unfortunately, no amount of remote troubleshooting can resolve a physical break. We will need to dispatch a field technician.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Oh, great. How long is that going to take?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I've just pulled up the master ticket for your area. Our line crew has already been dispatched to investigate the outage. I am adding your specific account to this ticket right now. The current Estimated Time to Repair, or ETR, is four to six hours.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Four to six hours? Wow. Okay. I guess there's no way around it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm afraid not. In the meantime, I do see that your corporate account includes 25 mobile lines with us. Do you have your Cymbal Telecom work mobile with you?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, I do.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You should be able to use your phone's personal hotspot feature to get your computer online. Our 5G network is quite robust and should be more than enough for emails and even uploading your report.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You know, I completely forgot about that. That's a great idea. Yes, I know how to turn on the hotspot. That should get me through.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. So, just to recap: we've confirmed a physical fiber line break in your area, likely from the storm. A repair crew is already dispatched with an estimated repair time of four to six hours. Your account is linked to the outage ticket, and you'll receive an automated text message once service is restored. In the meantime, you can use your mobile hotspot.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay. That covers everything. Thanks for figuring it out and for the hotspot reminder.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are very welcome, Mr. Taylor. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, that's it for me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alright. We appreciate your patience while our crews work to get you back online. Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom, and have a better rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Thanks, you too. Bye.
